source: បច្ចេកទេស ដាំដុះដំណាំដំឡូងជ្វា (Sweet Potato Cultivation Techniques), MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, 2018
text:
Sweet potato is a perennial-type vining crop with the following morphological characteristics:

Vine (stem): A creeping vine typically 2-3 meters long.

Root/tuber: Roots spread out along the vine and swell into tubers, occurring in a range of flesh and skin colors.

Leaf: Leaves vary in shape, some heart-shaped and some lobed, with color ranging from green to reddish depending on variety.

Flower: Flower color varies by variety, including purple, white, and pink, blooming at the tip of the vine or at leaf axils.

Fruit/seed: Sweet potato does not produce abundant seed pods; some varieties produce fruit near the vine tip after flowering, but seed is not reliable for propagation or variety identification, since sweet potato is propagated vegetatively from vine cuttings rather than from seed.

Growing season: In Cambodia, farmers generally plant sweet potato from around August through November-December, and it is possible to grow two crops per year, with an earlier planting sometimes starting as early as the third lunar month or as late as May, depending on water availability and local practice.
